candidates.arm_up: 0.99 (+0.025, mirror of JT's step; new build: tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 with the exp70g knobs + --set READMIT_MIN_SCORE=0.99)
candidates.arm_down: 0.94 (-0.025 = JT 743929 step; already built and dummy-gated as experiments/exp85c_k2cap6_ra094, PASS +0.84% nodes, 82 forks)
candidates.mechanism: Readmit (c07 readmit_discarded_detections) adds back free lowdet peaks with score >= READMIT_MIN_SCORE within 4 um of an open track end (t-1 node with no out-edge) or start (t+1 node with no in-edge); the second relink then attaches them 1:1 or they are pruned as isolated. lowdet peaks come from the same fused map and the same NMS kernel as the ILP candidates, so at 0.965 the pool is exactly the ILP-DROPPED candidates next to an open end; 0.94 adds sub-threshold peaks in [0.94,0.965). Each surviving readmit closes a track break (fragment end -> readmit -> fragment start), i.e. it re-wires which edges exist: a TP edge pair if the peak is a real nucleus, an FP edge (and possibly a wrong continuation) if it is a duplicate or debris. The up arm keeps only readmits the detector was sure of (the >= 0.99 band holds 75% of readmits) and removes the least confident quarter. Coupling: the value is also the LOWREFINE threshold (_LOWREFINE_MIN_SCORE). On the up arm, pool peaks in [0.965,0.99) stay on the 4-px grid, but only readmits (dropped anyway) and gapfill nodes (0.09% of nodes) use pool coordinates, so the coupling is close to inert. On the down arm it is coherent, because band readmits get head coordinates.
candidates.expected_output_change: exp60 lab (56 clips, CPU; the 14,525 presafe readmits matched exactly to lowdet peaks): readmits are 1.26% of nodes, 13,284 survive to final (1.18%) and touch 16,677 final edges (1.54%). Score histogram of readmits: [0.965,0.98) 1,653, [0.98,0.99) 1,975, >= 0.99 10,897. So arm_up 0.99 = -3,628 nodes (-0.32%), with about 0.4% of edges re-wired (dummy estimate about -340 of 1,365 readmits on 121,252 nodes = -0.28%). The LOWREFINE refined count drops about 8% (lowdet [0.965,0.99) = 106,622 of 1.34M peaks), which does not change the output except gapfill coordinates. arm_down 0.94: +6,303 free band peaks within 4 um of an open end in the lab (+0.55%, matching F-TRN-55 +0.60%); dummy exp85c +1,022 nodes (+0.84%), LOWREFINE +3.05%, forks 81 -> 82. Both arms are inside 1.5%.
candidates.runtime_risk: None measurable: readmit is one KD-tree query per frame, and the exp85c dummy took 1,736 s, within the range of the other K2 dummies. The up arm refines fewer peaks, so it is slightly faster.
candidates.evidence: 743929, John Taylor, on his x138 fork: 0.965 -> 0.94 = +0.001 (0.958 -> 0.959), node change < 1%, 0 of 2,212 annotated local edges changed, so his lab could not see it. Our P50 (exp85a = ILP 0.4 + READMIT 0.94) is pending and mixes the two JT knobs; exp85c isolates the down arm. Nobody has read the up arm (0.99). It is the other half of JT's two-arm read and tells whether the readmit gain comes from lower-score peaks (then step down to 0.92, as in exp86c) or whether 0.965 is already past the optimum. Lab (F-TRN-55): readmitted nodes are 3.5-6x depleted near GT (in-sample, recall-blind), so the lab cannot sign this knob. Files: experiments/exp85c_k2cap6_ra094/probe.json; research/KNOWLEDGE/FACTS.md F-TRN-55, F-TRN-56, F-MOD-43.

candidates.arm_up: 0.97 (+0.005; in the cell-1 guard, which the builder patches for --set keys)
candidates.mechanism: Candidate threshold on the fused dual-seed/TTA detection map inside the predict subprocess. It is also the threshold of the per-frame dual-seed retention guard (the primary vs blended map switch), so its effect is nonlinear. It changes the ILP's node set and so which ILP edges and probabilities exist; the flow relink then rebuilds all edges 1:1 on the new node set. Down arm: more low-confidence candidates compete in the ILP and in the relink, re-wiring edges in dense regions. Up arm: peaks in [0.965,0.97) leave the ILP, but readmit can bring them back (READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965 < 0.97) where they sit next to an open end. So the up arm turns marginal detections from ILP candidates into readmit-only peaks, which re-wires edges rather than purging nodes.
candidates.expected_output_change: exp60 lowdet bands (same map and NMS as the candidates): [0.955,0.965) 18,596 and [0.965,0.975) 26,450 of 1,341,252 candidates. Down arm: about +9.3k candidates (+0.7%); final nodes estimated +0.4-0.6% after ILP selection (the ILP drops about 13% of all candidates, preferring to drop low-score ones). Up arm: about -13k candidates (-1.0%); final nodes estimated -0.5-0.8% after readmit returns band peaks near open ends. These estimates assume a flat score density within each 0.01 band.
candidates.runtime_risk: Low: +/-0.7-1% candidates changes ILP and relink time in proportion (minutes on a 7-7.8 h run). The down arm is the slower one.
candidates.evidence: imissher 743222 on the 0.947 stack (same detector family, same 0.965 default): 0.960 -> 0.946 and 0.970 -> 0.945 vs unmodified 0.946/0.948, 'both directions lose, 0.965 at optimum'. That is already a two-arm read on a close ancestor. Our P04 exp19 (0.95) on the old 0.941 pipeline was neutral. x138 adds readmit, gapfill and the flow relink, which change how marginal peaks are used, so the ancestor's read may not transfer. Still, it is the only disclosed read and it is negative. Worth a slot only after the READMIT arms are used up.

candidates.mechanism: Flip-TTA averaging of the DeepCenter centre heatmap. That heatmap scores (a) synthetic gap-middle nodes on gaps >= 8.5 um (threshold 0.25) and (b) every new safe-division daughter (threshold 0.25). With TTA off the single-view scores are noisier, so marginal forks and gap closes flip at random in both directions. The effect lands on the division terms of the metric, because safe divisions are the main source of forks (safe divisions OFF = 0.911 vs 0.947).
candidates.expected_output_change: exp60 lab (TTA on): 6,617 safe-division DeepCenter checks, 1,763 accepted, 804 (12%) within +-0.025 of the 0.25 threshold, so a few hundred checks could flip. Accepted forks are then capped, so the final fork change is probably a few percent of the ~80 forks per 4-clip dummy; node count change << 0.1%. Gap-veto flips were not measured (they affect only marginal synthetic gaps of >= 8.5 um).
candidates.runtime_risk: Negative (it skips the TTA passes of the DeepCenter scorer, saving minutes).
candidates.evidence: Inherited from sjlee dctta (P14 exp29 0.947) and never varied on its own. Our DeepCenter safe-div threshold axis is closed with both directions losing (0.30 -> 0.949, 0.20/0.225 -> 0.954 vs the family best of 0.956), so the veto sits at a tuned optimum. Turning TTA off perturbs that veto in no particular direction, so the expected sign is negative. Listed to complete the detection group, and as a runtime lever if a later file needs time headroom.

summary: Group detection + readmit/lowrefine: only READMIT_MIN_SCORE is a strong two-arm candidate. Its arms are up 0.99 (new; -0.32% nodes, drops the least confident quarter of the 14,525 lab readmits) and down 0.94 (JT +0.001 on x138; already built as exp85c, dummy +0.84%). DET_THRESHOLD 0.97/0.96 is live and within the node budget (+0.7% / -1.0% candidates), but imissher (743222) already read both directions as losses on the 0.947 stack, so its prior is low. DEEPCENTER_TTA=0 has only one arm and randomly perturbs a closed veto axis, so its prior is low; it is useful only as a runtime lever. Rejected with CPU evidence from the exp60 lab dumps (56 clips): NMS pool_kernel_um is not an env knob, and 5.0 um sits on the (3,3,3) plateau that covers 2.44-5.69 um; the only moves are kernel 1 (node explosion) or kernel 5 (>= 3.3% of candidates suppressed). GAPFILL_EXCLUDE_UM is inert for readmit (7 eligible peaks in the (1.5,3] um band across 56 clips), and gapfill nodes are 0.09% of all nodes. GAPFILL_PEAK_RADIUS_UM is too small to matter for the same reason (gapfill = 0.09% of nodes). LOWDET_THRESHOLD is inert in [0,0.5], LOWREFINE_ENABLE was LB-tested in P38, and UNET_BATCH_SIZE only affects runtime. Notes: research/wf_ideas_v4/knobarms_28sep/arms_1.notes.md.
